setting: # The General Roman Calendar (the Roman Missal, 2002, with the calendar as
# it stands in 2026).  Any setting from config.csv may be given here and wins
# over it for this tradition.  See docs/traditions.md.
# Which celebration is kept when two fall together, by the Table of
# Liturgical Days: a solemnity that is impeded moves to the next free day
# anything lesser that is impeded is not kept that year.
# Solemnities are "principal", feasts "festivals", for the Feasts menu.
# Precedence settles the conflicts, so a feast is never drawn in the lower
# half of a greater day as the LCMS calendar does.
# The Bible version the page opens readings in (bible_version).
# The Lectionary for Mass, Years A, B and C (Year A from Advent 2025): data/readings/roman.csv, shared with Divine Worship (data/Anglican).
# The weekdays (data/readings/roman-weekday.csv): Ordinary Time's first reading and psalm in cycle I in odd years, II in even (Year II from Advent 2025).
# The Proper of Saints (data/readings/roman-saints.csv): the feasts not in roman.csv and the memorials with proper readings.

value: ot=First Reading; psalm=Responsorial Psalm; epistle=Second Reading; procession=Gospel at the Procession

setting: # The readings are cited as the NABRE numbers them (the Hebrew way); links in another version translate them (docs/versification.md).
# A weekday without a name of its own is named for the week its Sunday begins: Tuesday of the Sixth Week of Easter.

# Hymnary.org's code for Worship, fourth edition (GIA, 2011), one of the Catholic hymnals in wide use in the United States: a hymn mark after each set of readings searches it (hymnary.org/hymnal/WORS2011).
